items.stem: What is a salary?
options: A percentage of the value of sales
A fixed amount paid per year, usually in equal monthly parts
items.answer: A fixed amount paid per year, usually in equal monthly parts
items.markingKey: Salary: annual amount; wages are paid per hour worked.

items.stem: Explain the difference between gross pay and net pay.
items.answer: Gross pay is the total earned before deductions; net pay is what is left after deductions such as tax and pension have been taken off.
items.markingKey: B1 gross before deductions; B1 net after deductions [2]

items.stem: Explain why a salesperson might prefer a lower basic wage with commission to a higher fixed wage.
items.answer: If they make many sales, commission can make total pay higher than the fixed wage; their pay rewards their effort.
items.markingKey: B1 commission increases with sales; B1 can exceed fixed wage [2]

items.stem: A bus driver in Lima is paid $9.00 per hour for a basic 38-hour week. Overtime on weekdays is paid at time and a half. One week they work 38 basic hours, 7.5 hours of weekday overtime. Calculate their gross pay.

A gardener in Karachi is paid $16.40 per hour for a basic 40-hour week. Overtime on weekdays is paid at time and a half and on Sundays at double time. One week they work 40 basic hours, 3 hours of weekday overtime and 2 hours on Sunday. Calculate their gross pay.

Tariq works as a lifeguard in Accra. The basic rate is $13.50 per hour for 40 hours a week, with overtime at time and a half. One week Tariq works 45 hours. Each week the first $250.00 of pay is tax-free, the rest is taxed at 20%, and 4% of gross pay is deducted for insurance. (a) Calculate the tax paid. (b) Tariq is offered an annual salary of $34,300.00 instead. Assuming the same hours every week for 52 weeks, state with a reason which option gives the higher gross pay.
items.answer: (a) $78.25 (b) The salary (hourly gives $33,345.00 a year)

items.stem: What is commission?
options: Pay calculated as a percentage of the value of sales made
items.answer: Pay calculated as a percentage of the value of sales made
items.markingKey: Sales staff often earn commission on top of a basic wage.

items.stem: Explain why a person paid a salary does not receive more money for working extra hours, while a person on an hourly wage does.
items.answer: A salary is a fixed amount for the year whatever the hours; a wage is paid per hour, so extra hours (often at overtime rates) increase pay.
items.markingKey: B1 salary fixed; B1 wage per hour [2]

items.stem: Explain what a tax-free allowance is and how it affects the tax paid.
items.answer: It is the amount of income on which no tax is charged; tax is only paid on income above the allowance.
items.markingKey: B1 untaxed amount; B1 tax on remainder only [2]

items.stem: Diego is paid $12.00 per hour for the first 35 hours each week and time and a half for any extra hours. Diego works 41 hours and says the pay is 41 × $18.00 = $738.00. Explain the error and calculate the correct pay.
items.answer: Only the 6 extra hours are paid at time and a half; the first 35 hours are at the normal rate. Correct pay = $528.00.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies that only overtime hours get 1.5 ×; M1 35 × 12 + 6 × 18; A1 $528.00 [3]

items.stem: Ethan sells solar panels and earns a basic £350.00 per week plus 5% commission on all sales. One week Ethan sells £15,200.00 worth of solar panels. Calculate Ethan's total pay for the week.
Sofia sells solar panels and earns a basic $320.00 per week plus 2.5% commission on all sales. One week Sofia sells $4,800.00 worth of solar panels. Calculate Sofia's total pay for the week.

Ravi works as a bus driver in Santiago. The basic rate is €15.80 per hour for 40 hours a week, with overtime at time and a half. One week Ravi works 48 hours. Each week the first €200.00 of pay is tax-free, the rest is taxed at 12%, and 2% of gross pay is deducted for insurance. (a) Calculate the tax paid. (b) Calculate the net pay as a percentage of the gross pay.

Lucas works as a hotel receptionist in Muscat. The basic rate is €12.40 per hour for 40 hours a week, with overtime at time and a half. One week Lucas works 48 hours. Each week the first €250.00 of pay is tax-free, the rest is taxed at 15%, and 4% of gross pay is deducted for insurance. (a) Calculate the gross pay for the week. (b) Calculate the net pay as a percentage of the gross pay.
Which formula gives simple interest I on principal P at rate r% per year for n years?
items.answer: I = Prn/100
items.markingKey: Simple interest is the same each year: P × r/100 × n.

items.stem: Explain why compound interest gives more than simple interest at the same rate after several years.
items.answer: With compound interest, interest is earned on previous interest as well as the principal, so the amount added grows each year; simple interest adds the same amount each year.
items.markingKey: B1 interest on interest; B1 simple interest constant [2]

items.stem: Explain why after 1 year simple and compound interest give the same amount.
items.answer: In the first year both calculate interest on the original principal only; the difference starts once interest is added to the balance.
items.markingKey: B1 both on principal in year 1; B1 difference from year 2 [2]

items.stem: Zara invests €6,000.00 at 5% per year compound interest. Calculate the value of the investment after 8 years.
Nadia invests $2,400.00 in a bank in Manila at 4% per year compound interest. Calculate the total interest earned after 4 years.
Omar invests $1,500.00 in a bank in Mumbai at 5% per year compound interest. Calculate the total interest earned after 8 years.

Elena has $3,000.00 to invest in Cairo. Bank A offers 3.5% per year simple interest. Bank B offers 2.9% per year compound interest. (a) Calculate the total value with Bank B after 8 years. (b) State which bank gives more after 8 years and by how much.
items.answer: (a) $3,770.89 (b) Bank A (simple), by $69.11

items.stem: Mei has $10,000.00 to invest in Accra. Bank A offers 5% per year simple interest. Bank B offers 4.4% per year compound interest. (a) Calculate the total value with Bank B after 8 years. (b) Find the least number of complete years after which Bank B is worth more than Bank A.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 10000 × 1.044⁸; A1 $14,112.50 [2] (b) M1 compares values year by year; A1 [3]

items.stem: Which formula gives the value A of P invested at r% compound interest for n years?
items.markingKey: Each year the value is multiplied by (1 + r/100).

items.stem: $1000 is invested at 5% compound interest per year. What is the value after 2 years?
Explain what the number 1.035 represents in the calculation 2000 × 1.035⁴.
items.answer: It is the multiplier for an increase of 3.5% each year (100% + 3.5%).
items.markingKey: B1 multiplier; B1 3.5% increase per year [2]

items.stem: Tariq wants the value of $2,000.00 after 5 years at 6% compound interest and types 2000 × 6⁵ into a calculator. Explain the error and find the correct value.
items.answer: The multiplier for a 6% increase is 1.06, not 6: 2000 × 1.06⁵ = $2,676.45.
items.markingKey: B1 multiplier should be 1 + r/100; M1 correct calculation; A1 $2,676.45 [3]

items.stem: Freya invests $3,500.00 at 3% per year compound interest for 3 years and calculates the final amount as 3500 × (1 + 3 × 3 ÷ 100) = $3,815.00. Explain the error and find the correct amount.
items.answer: This is simple interest; compound interest multiplies by 1.03 each year: 3500 × 1.03³ = $3,824.54.
items.markingKey: B1 recognises simple interest used; M1 3500 × 1.03³; A1 $3,824.54 [3]

items.stem: Lucas invests $3,000.00 at 4.5% per year compound interest. Calculate the value of the investment after 5 years.
Aisha invests $1,200.00 at simple interest. After 3 years the interest earned is $108.00. Calculate the rate of interest per year.
Amara invests €4,500.00 at 2.5% per year compound interest. Calculate the value of the investment after 8 years.
Yusuf invests $800.00 at simple interest. After 2 years the interest earned is $40.00. Calculate the rate of interest per year.

Felix has €8,000.00 to invest in Lagos. Bank A offers 3.5% per year simple interest. Bank B offers 3% per year compound interest. (a) Calculate the total value with Bank B after 8 years. (b) Explain why Bank B eventually overtakes Bank A even though its rate is lower.
items.answer: (a) €10,134.16 (b) Compound interest grows exponentially (interest on interest) while simple interest grows by a fixed amount each year.

items.stem: Ravi has $5,000.00 to invest in Hanoi. Bank A offers 3.5% per year simple interest. Bank B offers 3% per year compound interest. (a) Calculate the total value with Bank A after 5 years. (b) Explain why Bank B eventually overtakes Bank A even though its rate is lower.
items.answer: (a) $5,875.00 (b) Compound interest grows exponentially (interest on interest) while simple interest grows by a fixed amount each year.

items.stem: A shop buys a lamp for $40 and sells it for $50. What is the percentage profit?
A price is increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%. Explain why it does not return to the original price.
items.answer: The 10% decrease is taken from the larger, increased price, so more is taken off than was added: 1.1 × 0.9 = 0.99, a 1% loss overall.
items.markingKey: B1 second percentage of a different amount; B1 overall multiplier 0.99 [2]

items.stem: Explain why you divide by 0.8, not multiply by 1.2, to find the original price of an item after a 20% discount.
items.answer: The sale price is 80% of the original, so original = sale price ÷ 0.8; adding 20% of the sale price uses the wrong base.
items.markingKey: B1 sale = 80% of original; B1 divide by 0.8 [2]

items.stem: The price of a kilogram of rice in Lima changed from $2.40 to $1.83. Calculate the percentage change, stating whether it is an increase or a decrease.
items.answer: 23.7% decrease

items.stem: The price of a smartwatch is €129.60 after a price rise of 8%. Calculate the price before the increase.

Ethan runs a market stall in Nairobi and buys 50 caps for $8.00 each. Ethan sells them at a 60% mark-up. After selling 40 of them, Ethan reduces the price of the rest by 40% and sells them all. (a) Calculate the original selling price of one item. (b) Calculate the total money received.
Which calculation gives the percentage change from an old value to a new value?
items.answer: (new − old) ÷ old × 100
items.markingKey: Percentage change is always relative to the original value.

items.stem: Explain why percentage profit is calculated using the cost price and not the selling price.
items.answer: Percentage profit measures the gain relative to the amount spent (the original value), which is the cost price.
items.markingKey: B1 relative to original; B1 cost price is original [2]

items.stem: In a sale, a bicycle costs £45.00 after a 40% discount. Ines finds the original price by adding 40% of £45.00 and gets £63.00. Explain why this is wrong and find the original price.
items.answer: The discount was 40% of the original price, not of the sale price. Sale price = 60% of original, so original = 45 ÷ 0.6 = £75.00.
items.markingKey: B1 percentage of the wrong amount; M1 ÷ 0.6; A1 £75.00 [3]

items.stem: In a sale, a bicycle costs $45.00 after a 25% discount. Sipho finds the original price by adding 25% of $45.00 and gets $56.25. Explain why this is wrong and find the original price.
items.answer: The discount was 25% of the original price, not of the sale price. Sale price = 75% of original, so original = 45 ÷ 0.75 = $60.00.
items.markingKey: B1 percentage of the wrong amount; M1 ÷ 0.75; A1 $60.00 [3]

items.stem: A shop buys pair of bootss for $18.00 each and marks the price up by 40%. In a sale the marked price is reduced by 15%. Calculate the sale price and the overall percentage profit.
items.answer: Sale price $21.42; profit 19.0%

items.stem: The price of a scooter is $768.00 including sales tax of 20%. Calculate the price before the increase.

Arjun runs a market stall in Dhaka and buys 50 scarves for £7.50 each. Arjun sells them at a 40% mark-up. After selling 30 of them, Arjun reduces the price of the rest by 30% and sells them all. (a) Calculate the total money received. (b) Calculate the overall percentage profit.

Arjun runs a market stall in Kathmandu and buys 80 water bottles for £12.00 each. Arjun sells them at an 80% mark-up. After selling 64 of them, Arjun reduces the price of the rest by 40% and sells them all. (a) Calculate the total money received. (b) Calculate the overall percentage profit.
Which multiplier represents an increase of 4% each year?
Explain the difference between a quantity decreasing by $500 each year and one decreasing by 10% each year.
items.answer: A fixed $500 decrease is linear (same amount each year); a 10% decrease is exponential, so the amount lost each year gets smaller as the value falls.
items.markingKey: B1 linear vs exponential; B1 amount lost changes [2]

items.stem: Explain why a population growing by 5% per year does not double in 20 years.
items.answer: Compound growth: 1.05²⁰ ≈ 2.65, so it more than doubles; 20 × 5% = 100% would only apply to simple (linear) growth.

items.stem: A culture of bacteria starts with 500 cells and the number increases by 30% every hour. Calculate the number of cells after 5 hours, to the nearest whole number.
A new car costs $18,500. Its value depreciates by 12% each year. Calculate its value after 4 years.

Arjun buys a laptop in Mexico City for $1200. Its value falls by 30% each year. (a) Calculate the total percentage loss in value over 4 years. (b) Find the first year in which its value is less than $300.
A quantity increases by 15% each year. Which number should it be multiplied by each year?
Explain why the graph of the value of a car that depreciates by 15% per year is a curve and not a straight line.
items.answer: The value is multiplied by 0.85 each year, so the yearly decrease gets smaller; the rate of change is not constant.
items.markingKey: B1 multiplied by constant factor; B1 decreasing drops/non-constant gradient [2]

items.stem: The number of visitors to a museum in Madrid grew from 12,000 to 13,498 in 3 years. The number increased by the same percentage each year. Calculate this percentage.
The number of visitors to a museum in Doha grew from 12,000 to 15,117 in 3 years. The number increased by the same percentage each year. Calculate this percentage.
The number of visitors to a museum in Singapore grew from 8,000 to 10,210 in 5 years. The number increased by the same percentage each year. Calculate this percentage.
A new car costs $26,000. Its value depreciates by 12% each year. Calculate its value after 3 years.

Arjun buys a laptop in Cape Town for $800. Its value falls by 35% each year. (a) Calculate its value after 2 years. (b) Find the first year in which its value is less than $200. (c) Arjun says the laptop loses $280 every year. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: (a) $338.00 (b) Year 4 (c) The 35% is taken from the current (falling) value, so the amount lost decreases each year.

items.stem: Gross pay is
options: pay after tax has been taken off
items.answer: total pay before any deductions
items.markingKey: Net pay = gross pay − deductions (tax, pension, insurance).

items.stem: Amara is paid €13.50 per hour for the first 38 hours each week and time and a half for any extra hours. Amara works 46 hours and says the pay is 46 × €20.25 = €931.50. Explain the error and calculate the correct pay.
items.answer: Only the 8 extra hours are paid at time and a half; the first 38 hours are at the normal rate. Correct pay = €675.00.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies that only overtime hours get 1.5 ×; M1 38 × 13.5 + 8 × 20.25; A1 €675.00 [3]

items.stem: Amara earns $41,000.00 per year. Income tax is not paid on the first $10,000.00 and is 20% on the rest. Calculate the amount of tax Amara pays each year and the net annual pay.
Freya earns $52,000.00 per year. Income tax is not paid on the first $15,000.00 and is 18% on the rest. Calculate the amount of tax Freya pays each year and the net annual pay.

Each week the first $150.00 of pay is tax-free, the rest is taxed at 15%, and 3% of gross pay is deducted for insurance. (a) Calculate the gross pay for the week. (b) Calculate the net pay as a percentage of the gross pay.
Compound interest is interest that is
options: only paid once at the end
paid on the original amount and on interest already earned
paid only on the original amount
items.answer: paid on the original amount and on interest already earned
items.markingKey: Interest is added to the balance, which then earns interest itself.

items.stem: Lina wants the value of $2,000.00 after 6 years at 3% compound interest and types 2000 × 3⁶ into a calculator. Explain the error and find the correct value.

items.stem: Leila wants the value of €5,000.00 after 5 years at 6% compound interest and types 5000 × 6⁵ into a calculator. Explain the error and find the correct value.

items.markingKey: B1 multiplier should be 1 + r/100; M1 correct calculation; A1 €6,691.13 [3]

items.stem: Grace invests €1,200.00 at simple interest. After 3 years the interest earned is €144.00. Calculate the rate of interest per year.

items.stem: A machine worth $18,000 depreciates by 15% per year. Kenji says that after 5 years it has lost 75% of its value, so it is worth $4,500.00. Explain the mistake and find the correct value.
items.answer: Each year 15% is taken from the reduced value, so the losses are not simply added: value = 18000 × 0.85⁵ = $7,986.70.
items.markingKey: B1 depreciation is compound; M1 18000 × 0.85⁵; A1 $7,986.70 [3]

items.stem: A machine worth $15,000 depreciates by 15% per year. Omar says that after 3 years it has lost 45% of its value, so it is worth $8,250.00. Explain the mistake and find the correct value.
